one_liner: Meta's enterprise-grade APIs for WhatsApp business messaging and calling.

evidence.claim: API requests authenticate with a Bearer access token in the Authorization header
evidence.quote: Bearer token for API authentication. This should be a valid access token obtained through the appropriate OAuth flow or system user token.

evidence.claim: Platform docs state authentication uses OAuth-style access tokens with permissions scoping
evidence.quote: Authentication uses OAuth (not 2.0) access tokens, while permissions restrict access to specific resources.

evidence.claim: Self-serve onboarding: free Meta developer registration and app creation yields credentials
evidence.quote: registering as a developer, creating a Meta app, sending your first message, and setting up a test webhook endpoint

evidence.claim: Developers can immediately generate a test access token and send messages without payment
evidence.quote: Click Generate access token to generate a temporary access token to send a test message.

evidence.claim: REST-style API built on Meta's Graph API over HTTP, spanning multiple sub-APIs
evidence.quote: The WhatsApp Business Platform is built on Graph API and uses HTTP protocol.

notes: Platform comprises multiple APIs: Cloud API (messages, calls, groups), Business Management API (WABA assets), Marketing Messages API, plus webhooks and an official OpenAPI spec and Postman collection—broad surface. Gotchas: the generated token is temporary (permanent tokens require creating a system user); going live at scale requires a real phone number, business verification, and App Review for permissions; per-message pricing applies to template/marketing messages though customer-service-window messages are free; conversation-based pricing was deprecated July 1, 2025. Docs oddly state 'OAuth (not 2.0)'. No official MCP server is mentioned in the supplied material.
